flow.costPlain: Running Snowflake's platform — data centers and the cost of delivering its product and services.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 20% YoY — growing, but slower than revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 35% YoY — the fastest-growing cost line.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 40% YoY.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $139.19 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — while other income added $5.74 and a tax benefit added $0.44, leaving a $33.01 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $986,770K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $92.8M (a 9% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $386.7M, other income covered $56.6M of that and a tax benefit added $4.3M, so the chart draws the remaining $325.7M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source.
oneTimers: A $1.9M restructuring charge for a restructuring plan at a majority-owned subsidiary, booked inside operating results and excluded from non-GAAP results.
$3.0M of expenses associated with acquisitions and strategic investments, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $56.6M, net: $56.3M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, less $2.1M of interest expense and plus $2.4M of other income, net. Income tax was a $4.3M benefit. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $327.5M (EPS -$0.99), after $1.8M of income attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 28% YoY and 96% of all revenue; product gross profit was $670.1M, a 71% margin.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 19% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (a $16.5M gross loss).

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 28% to $943.3M, the net revenue retention rate was 126%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 33% to $6.9B. Snowflake guided Q1 FY26 product revenue to $955–$960M, up 21–22%, at a 5% non-GAAP operating margin.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $386.7M. The main reason: $449.1M of stock-based compensation-related charges, including employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $92.8M, a 9% margin.
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 580 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+27% YoY) and 745 Forbes Global 2000 customers. Operating cash flow was $432.7M and adjusted free cash flow was $423.1M.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 27% to $986.8M, with product revenue up 28% to $943.3M — but $449.1M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $386.7M and a net loss of $325.7M.
